question: By selling an article at 6/15 of its actual selling price, Nirbhay incurs a loss of 14%. If he sells it at 54% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling at 6/15 (or 40%) of Actual SP gives a 14% loss (which is 86% of CP).

⇒ 40% of Actual SP = 86% of CP

⇒ 1% of Actual SP = 2.15% of CP

⇒ 54% of Actual SP = 54 × 2.15% of CP = 116.1% of CP

⇒ Profit = 116.1% − 100% = 16.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price is 6/15 of the Actual SP and loss is 14%.

New Selling Price is 54% of the Actual SP.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100.

⇒ At a 14% loss, Initial Selling Price = 100 − 14 = 86

⇒ Initial SP = 6/15 × Actual SP

⇒ 86 = 2/5 × Actual SP

⇒ Actual SP = 86 × 5 ÷ 2 = 215

⇒ New Selling Price = 54% of Actual SP

⇒ New SP = (54 ÷ 100) × 215 = 116.1

⇒ Profit % = New SP − CP

⇒ Profit % = 116.1 − 100 = 16.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit or loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) after a discount is calculated as SP = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100.

Relationship between CP, SP and MP

A direct relationship combining profit and discount is: CP × (100 + Profit %) = MP × (100 − Discount %).
